notation: Logical Arabic in the engine notation (engines.ff4_arabic): a line for each page of the message (the box shows four rows of 26 cells; the game waits for the button between pages), {line} where a row must end, {blank} for an empty row; the encoder breaks the other rows itself, a word at a time. {Name 00} writes a character's name: the entries name.00 to name.0D give the fourteen characters' names in Arabic (Cecil first), which the hook writes in place of the name the player gave; a row counts six cells for a name. {Song 2A}, {Wait 10} and {Gil} pass to the game as the English has them, and {Close} at the very end closes the window at once. A message holds Arabic letters, spaces, Western or Arabic-Indic digits and the signs . , : ! - … ' % / ، ؛ ؟ only. No vowel marks: the font has none.

Crewmen talk among themselves: why are they robbing crystals from innocent people; that is their duty; do they really have to keep doing this
entries.text:
الطاقم:لماذا نسلب البلورات من أناس أبرياء؟{line}الطاقم:هذا واجبنا.
الطاقم:هل علينا حقا أن نواصل فعل هذا؟

entries.context: The crew protests to the captain; Cecil ({Name 00}) answers that possessing the crystal is essential to the kingdom's prosperity, that the king judged the Mysidians know too much about its secret, that they are the Red Wings, the air force of Baron, and the royal command is absolute; the crew calls to him again

امتلاك البلورة عامل جوهري في ازدهارنا.{line}كما أن جلالته رأى أن أهل ميسيديا يعرفون الكثير
عن سر البلورة.{line}نحن الأجنحة الحمراء، سلاح الجو لمملكة بارون!{line}الأمر الملكي مطلق.
الطاقم:أيها القائد!

entries.context: A crewman cries out as monsters attack the airship
